seo.title: Holiday Merchant Center Checklist for Retailers
seo.meta_description: A holiday Merchant Center checklist for Orange County retailers: product data, shipping, returns, promotions, local inventory and issues, from Google's help.

h1: A Holiday Merchant Center Checklist for Orange County Retailers
answer: A holiday Merchant Center checklist covers the steps that keep products showing on Google during the busiest season: fix issues, keep prices and availability matching your site, add shipping and return policies, submit promotions early enough for Google's review and keep local inventory current. Anaheim and Orange County retailers who work through it before December avoid disapprovals when shoppers are searching most.
key_takeaways: Prices and availability must match your site.
Shipping is required in the U.S.

sections.heading: Why a checklist now
sections.body_html: Shoppers search for gifts across Google in November and December. Merchant Center decides whether your products can appear in free listings, Shopping ads and local listings, so problems found in mid-December cost sales. A checklist done now prevents that.

sections.heading: 1. Clear your issues
sections.body_html: Open Merchant Center's issues view. Google says disapproved products stop showing, while products with warnings may perform worse and can become disapproved. Fix account-level issues first, then the product issues affecting the most products.

sections.heading: 2. Match prices and availability
sections.body_html: Google says that when price or availability don't match between your product data and product pages, products can be pre-emptively disapproved and need a review. Holiday sales change prices often, so update product data automatically and frequently.

sections.heading: 3. Check the required product data
sections.body_html: Google's product data specification requires a title, description, image link, price and availability, with brand, GTIN and condition where they apply. Titles can be up to 150 characters. Rewrite titles for your best sellers so they say what the product is, with brand, size or color.

sections.heading: 4. Shipping and returns
sections.body_html: Google says shipping settings or costs are required in countries including the United States for free listings. It also recommends adding return policies, which can show next to products on ads, listings and Gmail. Set holiday return windows in Merchant Center as well as on your site.

sections.heading: 5. Submit promotions early
sections.body_html: Google reviews every promotion before it shows. Submit holiday promotions with a clean promotion ID, up to 50 characters with no spaces or symbols, and map them to the right products well before the sale starts.

sections.heading: 6. Keep local inventory current
sections.body_html: If you use free local listings or local inventory ads, Google says store codes must match your Business Profile, and syncing locations can take up to 24 hours. Update stock at least daily during the holidays.

sections.heading: 7. Plan for image requirements
sections.body_html: Google has announced that product images must be at least 500 x 500 pixels, enforced from January 31, 2027. Replace small images now, while you're already reviewing products.

sections.heading: The checklist
sections.body_html:
1. Clear account and product issues.
  2. Automate price and availability updates.
  3. Rewrite titles for top sellers.
  4. Confirm shipping settings.
  5. Upload return policies, including holiday terms.
  6. Submit promotions a week ahead.
  7. Update local inventory daily.
  8. Replace images under 500 x 500.

sections.heading: After the holidays
sections.body_html: Returns and new stock change what's accurate in January. Switch return policies back to normal terms, remove ended promotions and check issues again after the rush.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a gift shop in Orange with 300 products. In mid-November the owner clears 40 disapprovals caused by out-of-date prices, sets the product feed to update several times a day, adds a holiday return window, submits a December promotion a week early and updates the in-store inventory feed daily. Products keep showing through the busiest weeks.

sections.heading: Questions retailers ask us
sections.body_html: Retailers often ask what to do first if time is short. Clear issues on your best-selling products, then make sure prices and availability match your site. Another common question is whether promotions are worth the effort for small stores. For strong offers like holiday discounts or free shipping, yes, as long as they're submitted early enough for review. Retailers also ask about local inventory. If you have a store, showing in-stock items nearby can win last-minute shoppers who want a gift today.

sections.heading: Who does what during the holidays
sections.body_html: In a small store, holiday tasks often fall through the cracks because everyone is busy on the shop floor. Decide now who checks Merchant Center issues, who updates prices when sales start and end, who submits promotions and who keeps inventory accurate. Write the tasks on a simple calendar with dates, from mid-November to early January. Even if one person does everything, having the dates written down means nothing important is forgotten when the store is at its busiest and every hour counts.

sections.heading: Prepare for last-minute shoppers
sections.body_html: Many holiday shoppers leave gifts until the last week and want something today. If you have a physical store in Anaheim or elsewhere in Orange County, this is where accurate local inventory and pickup options pay off. Make sure your Business Profile shows extended holiday hours, your in-store stock is current and any same-day pickup option is clearly explained. Shoppers who see an item in stock nearby, with a store open late, often choose the local shop over waiting for delivery.

sections.heading: Keep a record for next year
sections.body_html: After the holidays, write down what worked and what didn't: which products sold best, which promotions made a difference, which issues caused problems and when. Note the dates you completed each checklist step. Next year, start from this record rather than from scratch. Over a few seasons, the checklist becomes a reliable routine tailored to your store, and the holiday rush becomes calmer and more profitable each year.

sections.heading: Check your website at the same time
sections.body_html: Merchant Center data reflects your website, so check the site alongside it. Make sure product pages load quickly on phones, sold-out items are marked as out of stock rather than deleted, holiday shipping cut-off dates are clearly shown and the checkout works smoothly with a real test order. Confirm that sale prices on product pages match your product data and structured data. Many Merchant Center issues start as small website problems, such as a slow page, a broken image or a price that didn't update, so fixing the site prevents issues before Google finds them. Run a quick test order on a phone each week until the new year to catch checkout problems early.

sections.heading: Use free listings before paying for ads
sections.body_html: If you're new to Merchant Center, start with free listings before spending on Shopping ads. Google says free listings can show products across Search, Maps, YouTube, Images, Lens and Gemini at no cost. Use the holiday season to learn which products get impressions and clicks, which titles work and which data problems come up. Once your product data is in good shape, you'll be in a much stronger position to decide whether ads are worth adding next year, and which products deserve the budget. For many small retailers, free listings alone bring useful extra visibility over the holidays.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Work through a holiday Merchant Center checklist before December: issues, prices, product data, shipping, returns, promotions, local inventory and images. Anaheim and Orange County retailers who do keep their products in front of holiday shoppers when it matters most.

faqs.q: What should a holiday Merchant Center checklist include?
faqs.a: Issues, prices and availability, product data, shipping, returns, promotions, local inventory and images.

faqs.q: Why do products get disapproved during sales?
faqs.a: Often because prices or availability don't match the product page.
